rationale: Both replace the byte-level state machine with a clear line-by-line renderer that tracks only whether a list is open, and both write good refactoring notes. A is a bit more precise and simpler. It treats a line as a list item only if it starts with '* ', and headerLevel reports cleanly whether a line is a header. It also keeps the four original strings.Replace calls, which are obvious at a glance. B matches any line starting with '*' as a list item and then only strips '* ', which is looser than intended. It also adds a hand-written replaceFirstPair helper that re-implements what strings.Replace(..., 1) already does, which is extra code with no benefit. B's switch statement is pleasant, but A's design is tighter and easier to trust.
